item.title: The First Dose That Slowed the Heart — Myriocin to Fingolimod-Phosphate S1P1 Agonism/Internalization (PDB 7EO4), Atrial GIRK First-Dose AV Block vs. Sustained Lymphocyte Sequestration & FREEDOMS/TRANSFORMS Trials
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology Pilot 107: Myriocin to Fingolimod-Phosphate S1P1 Agonism/Internalization (PDB 7EO4), Atrial GIRK First-Dose AV Block vs. Sustained Lymphocyte Sequestration & FREEDOMS/TRANSFORMS Trials. At the sixth hour of a first fingolimod observation, an atrial impulse reaches the ECG and fails to reach the ventricles. Two weeks later, the lab reports a sharp fall in circulating lymphocytes. The Critical Care Clinician follows conduction, perfusion and the blood count. The Molecular Pharmacologist follows an active phosphate ester into a receptor and then follows the receptor off the lymphocyte surface. The patient, dialogue and individual values are fictional. David S. Miller’s “ABC Transporter Regulation by Signaling at the Blood–Brain Barrier” (2014) in the live Pharmacology notebook provides the rat brain-capillary starting point. Drug development, human trials and bedside interpretation draw on separate sources. Pharmacology notebook · Primary capillary experiment

item.title: The Parkinson's Drug With Two Clocks — Axelrod's COMT Discovery, Nitrocatechol Tolcapone Mg2+ Coordination, Levodopa Wearing-Off Extension vs. Delayed Hepatotoxicity & Mitochondrial Uncoupling
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology Pilot 109: Axelrod's COMT Discovery, Nitrocatechol Tolcapone Mg2+ Coordination, Levodopa Wearing-Off Extension vs. Delayed Hepatotoxicity & Mitochondrial Uncoupling. A person with Parkinson’s disease gets part of his afternoon back. Ten weeks after adding tolcapone, he opens the same diary to write down when his urine darkened. The Critical Care Clinician reads the motor diary, then follows aminotransferases, bilirubin and INR. The Molecular Pharmacologist reconstructs COMT discovery, magnesium coordination and the evidence for a possible mitochondrial liability. The patient, test values and dialogue are fictional. The Pharmacology notebook anchor is the 2010 chapter *Biochemistry and Pharmacology of Catechol-O-Methyltransferase Inhibitors*, which reviews the recombinant human inhibition result. Pharmacology notebook · Notebook chapter

item.title: The Antibody That Took the Shuttle — Trontinemab Monovalent TfR1 Brainshuttle + Gantenerumab Fab (PDB 5CSZ), Centiloid Amyloid PET Clearance vs. Functional Endpoints (GRADUATE) & ARIA-E/ARIA-H MRI Surveillance

item.title: The Odor They Learned to Detect — Unilateral Nostril Androstenone Induction (Mainland 2002), Human OR7D4 Genetic Polymorphisms (Keller 2007) & Olfactory Training
item.description: Peripheral vs. central plasticity in human olfaction: Mainland et al.'s (2002) single-nostril exposure experiment showing contralateral transfer of acquired androstenone sensitivity, Keller et al.'s (2007) and Lunde et al.'s (2012) OR7D4 RT/WM receptor variants governing odor intensity and valence in pork taint, and Gillmeister et al.'s (2025) olfactory perceptual training.

item.title: The Pupil That Followed Imagined Light — Acquired Aphantasia (Zeman 2010), Objective Pupillary Light-Imagery Reflexes (Kay 2022), Object vs. Spatial Memory Drawings & Narrative Pupillometry
item.description: Physiological and behavioral measurement of visual mental imagery: Zeman et al.'s (2010) patient MX with acquired loss of voluntary imagery despite intact visual-perceptual tasks, Kay et al.'s (2022) pupillary constriction/dilation to imagined bright vs. dark triangles scaling with vividness and absent in aphantasia, Bainbridge et al.'s (2021) scene-drawing dissociation of object detail from intact spatial layout, and Vanbuckhave et al.'s (2026) spoken-story pupillometry.

item.title: The Click That Mapped the Room — Human Mouth-Click Echolocation Acoustics, Calcarine V1 Recruitment in Blind Experts (Thaler 2011), 10-Week Novice Training & Echo EEG
item.description: Acoustics and cross-modal cortical plasticity of human mouth-click echolocation: Thaler et al.'s (2017) beam-pattern and millisecond click measurements, Thaler et al.'s (2011) fMRI demonstration of calcarine visual-cortex echo-specific BOLD modulation in blind echolocators, Norman et al.'s (2021) 20-session training of blind and sighted novices across adulthood, and Garcia-Lazaro et al.'s (2026) EEG echo-evidence accumulation.

item.title: The Gorilla in the Scan — Radiologist Chest-CT Inattentional Blindness With Direct Gaze Fixation (Drew 2013), Simons & Chabris (1999), Fast-Motion Limits & Perceptual Sensitivity
item.description: Visual attention, expert search, and perceptual awareness boundaries: Simons & Chabris's (1999) selective-attention paradigm, Drew et al.'s (2013) lung-nodule chest-CT experiment in which 20 of 24 radiologists missed an embedded gorilla despite majority eye-tracking fixation on its location, Wallisch et al.'s (2023) motion-speed boundary conditions, and Nartker et al.'s (2025) large-scale test of residual visual sensitivity.

item.title: The Skill His Hands Kept — Henry Molaison's Robotic Force-Field Motor Retention Without Declarative Recall, Post-1953 Semantic Learning & 3D Postmortem Hippocampal Histology
item.description: Multiple human memory systems through quantitative testing of Patient H.M. (Henry Molaison): Scoville & Milner's (1957) surgical cohort, Shadmehr, Brandt & Corkin's robotic arm curl-field adaptation showing preserved motor-skill retention across days despite zero explicit recollection of the apparatus (Shadmehr & Krakauer 2008), O'Kane et al.'s (2004) sparse post-1953 semantic familiarity, and Annese et al.'s (2014) 2,401-slice histological brain reconstruction.

item.title: When the Pour Stood Still — Cerebral Akinetopsia in Patient L.M., Random-Dot Signal-to-Noise Breakdown (Baker 1991), Post-Stroke Smooth-Pursuit Eye Tracking & Speed-Selective Reversal
item.description: Selective loss and dissociation of human visual motion processing: Zihl & Heywood's (2015) clinical synthesis of bilateral V5/MT+ lesion patient L.M. ('frozen tea'), Baker et al.'s (1991) random-dot kinematogram demonstration of intact low-noise direction discrimination collapsing under visual noise, Cooper et al.'s (2012) unilateral stroke eye-tracking dissociation, and Heutink et al.'s (2019) patient T.D. speed-dependent motion reversal.

item.title: The Face She Knew by Voice — Posterior Cortical Atrophy Neuropsychological Profiles (H054), Serial Flower Drawings, Consensus Criteria & Amyloid/Autopsy Pathology

item.title: Reflexes, Recall, and Four Plastic Tubes — Bedside Neurologic Localization & HINTS vs. Early MRI (H053), Cognitive & Neuropsychological Storage-vs-Retrieval Profiling (H054) & Lumbar Puncture, 4-Tube Xanthochromia & CSF Signatures (H055)
item.description: Clinical Cluster & Clinical Neuroscience synthesis of standardized neurologic localization (H053), neuropsychological profiling (H054), and CSF analysis (H055): forehead-sparing CN VII, Romberg proprioception, FOUR Score, HINTS beating early DWI MRI, and Hoover sign; CVLT-3 storage vs. retrieval rescue, DLB haloperidol ban, TOPF norms, and TOMM validity; and Hasbun pre-LP CT + immediate antibiotics, 450-460 nm xanthochromia, CSF lactate, <72h HSV-1 PCR traps, and Lancet 2018 atraumatic needles (n=31,412).

item.title: Can a God Be Fooled? — Developmental False-Belief Tasks, Barrett's Cracker Box, Yukatek Maya Interviews & Omniscience vs. Moral Policing

item.title: How You Know Where Your Hand Is in the Dark — Goodwin's 100 Hz Tendon-Vibration Illusion, Ghez's Multi-Joint Reaching Without Proprioception, Woo's Piezo2 Spindles & Chesler's Human PIEZO2 Loss
item.description: From psychophysical illusions to the molecular mechanosensor of proprioception: Goodwin, McCloskey & Matthews (1972) tendon-vibration muscle-spindle illusions, Ghez et al. (1995) intersegmental dynamics defects in deafferented human reaching rescued partially by vision, Woo et al. (2015) conditional Piezo2 ablation silencing muscle-spindle Ia afferents, and Chesler et al. (2016) human PIEZO2 deficiency.

item.title: When the Lips Change the Sound You Hear — Sumby & Pollack's Speech-in-Noise Gain, McGurk & MacDonald's Ba/Ga→Da Fusion & Beauchamp's Superior Temporal Sulcus TMS Disruption
item.description: Multisensory speech integration and causal cortical testing: Sumby & Pollack (1954) audiovisual enhancement in noise across vocabulary set sizes, McGurk & MacDonald (1976) cross-modal syllable fusion where auditory /ba/ paired with lip-articulated /ga/ yields heard /da/, and Beauchamp, Nath & Pasalar (2010) fMRI-guided TMS over the superior temporal sulcus selectively reducing McGurk fusion while sparing congruent control syllables.

item.title: How a Burst Leaves a Synapse Stronger — Bliss & Lømo's 1973 Perforant-Path LTP Controls, Collingridge's APV NMDA Blockade & Tsien's CA1-Restricted NR1 Knockout

item.title: How Infants Tune In to Speech — Werker & Tees's 6-to-12-Month Head-Turn Narrowing, Maye's Bimodal vs. Unimodal Distributions, Kuhl's Live-vs.-Video Mandarin & Lytle's Peer Contingency

item.title: Who Knew What Was in the Box — Epistemic Access, Secret Ritual Objects, Theory-of-Mind Asymmetries & Religious Authority

item.title: Seven Seconds of Now — Patient H.M., Clive Wearing & How Memory Stitches Time
item.description: Unpacks Henry Molaison's 1953 medial temporal resection, Brenda Milner's mirror-star dissociation, Clive Wearing's 7-second diary, and hippocampal time cells.

item.title: The Sedative You Can Wake From — Dexmedetomidine Locus Coeruleus Alpha-2A Cryo-EM, GIRK Hyperpolarization, Vascular vs. Sympatholytic Biphasic Pressure & SPICE III / MENDS2 Trials

item.title: The Venom That Took the Spinal Route — Intrathecal Ziconotide (ω-Conotoxin MVIIA), Olivera's Conus magus Discovery, Human CaV2.2 Cryo-EM Pore Plug (PDB 7MIX) & Slow Titration
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology of intrathecal ziconotide (PRIALT / omega-conotoxin MVIIA): Olivera's discovery of Conus magus peptide toxins, Nieng Yan's 3.1 Å cryo-EM structure of human CaV2.2 plugged by ziconotide (PDB 7MIX), why systemic IV delivery causes orthostatic hypotension via sympathetic CaV2.2 block while intrathecal delivery targets dorsal horn lamina I/II synapses without tolerance or respiratory depression, and Staats (2004) vs. Rauck (2006) titration kinetics.

item.title: The Sedative the Screen Missed — GABAA alpha1-beta2-gamma2 Cryo-EM Allosteric Binding (6X3X/6X3U), Diazepam CYP2C19/3A4 vs. Lorazepam Direct UGT2B15 Glucuronidation & Why Urine Immunoassays Miss Lorazepam-Glucuronide
item.description: Receptor allostery, metabolic routing, and toxicology screen blind spots: cryo-EM structures of human alpha1-beta2-gamma2 GABAA receptors bound to diazepam (PDB 6X3X) and flumazenil (PDB 6X3U), Sternbach's benzodiazepine chemistry, diazepam CYP oxidation vs. lorazepam direct C3-OH glucuronidation, and why unhydrolyzed urine benzodiazepine immunoassays miss lorazepam-glucuronide without beta-glucuronidase hydrolysis and LC-MS/MS.

item.title: The Switch That Keeps Us Awake — Hypothalamic Orexin/Hypocretin Discovery, Canine HCRTR2 & Human CSF Orexin-A Deficiency in Narcolepsy Type 1, OX2R Crystal Structures (4S0V/7L1U) & Dual Orexin Receptor Antagonists
item.description: From wake-maintenance physiology to targeted insomnia pharmacology: 1998 discovery of hypothalamic hypocretins/orexins, 1999 canine HCRTR2 and murine knockout narcolepsy models, human CSF orexin-A <=110 pg/mL cutoff in ICSD-3 narcolepsy type 1, structural comparison of antagonist-bound (PDB 4S0V) vs. agonist-bound (PDB 7L1U) OX2R, and clinical trials and next-morning safety of suvorexant and daridorexant.

item.title: The Drug That Changed the Ward — Chlorpromazine from Rhône-Poulenc Patent & 1952 Psychiatric Wards (Laborit, Delay & Elkes) to Pause-Triggered Torsades, Human hERG Cryo-EM (5VA1), DRD2 Kinetics & Sulfoxide LC-MS/MS

item.title: The Breakfast That Changed a Bargain — Controlled 850-kcal Breakfast Crossovers in Ultimatum Bargaining (Strang 2017) vs. fMRI Risk Lotteries (Liu 2021), Plasma Tyrosine/LNAA & Human Tyrosine Hydroxylase Cryo-EM (6ZZU/6ZVP)
item.description: How acute macronutrient swaps in controlled 850-kcal breakfasts affect distinct economic decision tasks: Strang et al.'s (2017) Ultimatum Game crossover (unfair-offer rejection and plasma tyrosine/LNAA AUC) vs. Liu et al.'s (2021) fMRI monetary lottery crossover (overall behavioral null, fat-mass interaction, tryptophan/LNAA correlation, and parietal BOLD thresholds), grounded in human tyrosine hydroxylase cryo-EM structures (PDB 6ZZU apo & 6ZVP dopamine-bound).

item.title: The Amino Acid at the Brain's Gate — Six-Competitor Plasma Tryptophan Ratio, Human LAT1 Cryo-EM (8J8M/8XPU), TPH2 & PET Tracer Assumptions, Delgado's Remission Relapse Trials (14/21; 8/15 vs. 1/15) & Breakfast Limits
item.description: From plasma amino-acid competition at blood-brain barrier LAT1–CD98hc (PDB 8J8M L-Trp & 8XPU JPH203) to acute tryptophan depletion trials: UHPLC-MS/MS separation of isobaric Leu/Ile, recombinant TPH2 kinetics vs. alpha-[11C]methyl-L-Trp PET assumptions, Delgado's remitted depression crossover (14/21) and SSRI vs. desipramine responder split (8/15 vs. 1/15), and why Wurtman's breakfast study measured plasma ratios rather than mood.

item.title: When the Brain Burns Ketones — Drug-Resistant Pediatric Epilepsy, SCOT Succinyl-CoA Transferase (3DLX / 1OOY), [11C]Acetoacetate PET, Decanoate AMPA Block & the Neal Trial
item.description: From the 4:1 ketogenic diet ratio (90% energy from fat) and hepatic HMGCS2 ketogenesis to extrahepatic SCOT/OXCT1 glutamyl-CoA thioester catalysis (human apo PDB 3DLX vs. porcine Glu305 intermediate PDB 1OOY), dual [11C]acetoacetate/[18F]FDG brain PET, Chang et al. (2016) decanoic acid GluA2/GluA3 AMPA receptor antagonism, and Neal et al.'s (2008) randomized childhood epilepsy trial (145 randomized, 103 analyzed at 3 months).

item.title: The Side the Scalp Could See — Simultaneous Scalp vs. Stereo-EEG Seizure Detection (Gunnell 2025), 51-Second Contralateral Scalp Lag & ICU Peripheral Nerve Stimulator EEG Artifacts
item.description: Behind the Curtain of clinical electroencephalography (H045): simultaneous intracranial stereo-EEG and scalp EEG recordings showing a 51-second delay and false contralateral lateralization on the scalp (Nandkeolyar 2018; Gunnell et al. 2025 across 172 seizures), skull/tissue attenuation of deep focal discharges, and ICU peripheral nerve stimulator train-of-four artifacts mimicking seizures (Dhakal 2017).

item.title: The Pause That Finally Had a Time — Implantable Loop Recorder Asystole Masquerading as Epilepsy (Kanjwal 2010) vs. 38-Second Ictal Asystole on Simultaneous EEG/ECG (Nandkeolyar 2018), RAST Yield & Recorder Artifacts
item.description: Behind the Curtain of ambulatory ECG and implantable loop recording (H041): Kanjwal et al.'s (2010) loop-recorder capture of complete heart block and prolonged asystole causing convulsive syncope previously treated as epilepsy, contrasted with Nandkeolyar et al.'s (2018) simultaneous video-EEG/ECG capture of right temporal seizure onset preceding a 38-second ictal asystole, Krahn's randomized RAST diagnostic yield (14/27 vs. 6/30), and Domenichini's (2023) false-positive pause artifacts.

item.description: Behind the Curtain Diagnostics (H044) investigation of nocturnal dream-enactment mimics: how synchronized video-polysomnography (EEG, EOG, submental/limb EMG, nasal pressure, and thoracoabdominal effort belts) separates true alpha-synucleinopathy REM sleep behavior disorder (sustained/phasic REM sleep without atonia) from severe obstructive sleep apnea respiratory-arousal pseudo-RBD that resolves completely on CPAP (Deguchi et al. 2021; Bergmann et al. 2024).

item.description: Comparative auditory diagnostics across species (H050 & V034): Plonek's unilaterally deaf English Setter BAER waveforms and Lewis's 8,955-dog UK Dalmatian screening cohort (1,201 unilateral, 397 bilateral, 8 equivocal) paired with Starr's classic auditory neuropathy series and Eom's child with absent click ABR yet normal pure-tone thresholds and language.

item.title: The Seconds That Grew After the Fall — Stetson & Eagleman's 31-Meter Free-Fall Flicker Experiment, Oddball Predictability & Duration vs. Passage-of-Time Judgments
item.description: Experimental psychophysics of subjective time dilation and duration judgment: Stetson, Fiesta & Eagleman's (2007) 31-meter, 2.49-second free-fall experiment separating retrospective stopwatch expansion (2.96 s recalled vs. 2.17 s imagined, +36%) from unchanged wrist-LED flicker resolution, Pariyadath & Eagleman's (2007) visual oddball duration vs. pitch/flicker dissociation, and Martinelli & Droit-Volet's (2022, N=803) separation of numerical duration estimates from passage-of-time feelings.

item.title: How a Flash Test Separates the Retina’s Responses — Adrian's 1945 Red/Blue Scotopic-Photopic ERG, Dilated-Pupil Control, Miyake's Electronegative CSNB Waveform & ISCEV Standards
item.description: Retinal electrophysiology and clinical waveform dissection: Edgar Adrian's (1945) human corneal-thread ERG separating scotopic and photopic responses across wavelengths with dilated-pupil controls, Miyake et al.'s (1986, N=64) electronegative bright-flash ERG in congenital stationary night blindness (preserved photoreceptor a-wave with reduced ON-bipolar b-wave), and 2022 ISCEV full-field and On-Off ERG standards.

item.title: Why a Visual Signal Can Arrive Late After Sight Improves — Dawson's 1954 Signal Averaging, Halliday's 1972 Pattern-Reversal VEP in Optic Neuritis & Sokol's Dioptric Blur Artifact
item.description: Clinical neurophysiology of pattern-reversal Visual Evoked Potentials (VEP): Dawson's (1954) time-locked signal averaging, Halliday, McDonald & Mushin's (1972) discovery of persistent monocular cortical latency delay after visual acuity recovery in optic neuritis, and Sokol & Moskowitz's (1981) demonstration of refractive blur latency artifacts.

item.title: What an Ear Test Learns by Changing the Pressure — Terkildsen & Thomsen's 1959 Pressure Sweep, Jerger's 1970 Type A/B/C Curves, Equivalent Canal Volume & Infant 1,000 Hz Probes
item.description: Acoustic immittance physics and developmental biomechanics of tympanometry: Terkildsen & Thomsen's (1959) ear-canal pressure-sweep compliance peak, Jerger's (1970) Type A/B/C diagnostic classification, Mehta et al.'s (2006) equivalent ear-canal volume (Vec) three-way disambiguation of flat Type B traces, and Gellrich et al.'s (2024) myringotomy-validated proof of 1,000 Hz vs. 226 Hz probe tones in young infants.

item.title: How an Eye Scan Finds Layers with Light — Fercher's 1988 Low-Coherence Eye-Length Interferometry, Huang & Fujimoto's 1991 Retinal OCT & Preperimetric Glaucoma RNFL Loss
item.description: Optical physics and clinical translation of Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT): why femtosecond light propagation requires interferometric path-length matching rather than direct electronic clock timing, Fercher et al.'s (1988) low-coherence axial eye-length interferometry, Huang, Swanson & Fujimoto's (1991) cross-sectional retinal OCT invention, and Miki et al.'s (2014) longitudinal proof of structural RNFL thinning preceding visual field defects in glaucoma.

item.title: How a Nerve Test Finds Where a Signal Slows — Helmholtz's 1850 Two-Point Subtraction, Hodes's 1948 Human CMAP Velocity, Simpson/Gilliatt Focal Wrist Latency & Ring-Finger Comparison
item.description: Electrophysiology of clinical nerve conduction studies (H045): Helmholtz's (1850) two-point latency subtraction canceling synaptic and contractile delay, Hodes, Larrabee & German's (1948) percutaneous human compound muscle action potential (CMAP) conduction velocity method, Simpson (1956) and Gilliatt & Sears's (1958) localization of focal median nerve entrapment across the carpal tunnel, and Uncini et al.'s (1989) ring-finger median-vs-ulnar internal control.

item.title: How a Test Maps Vision Away from Where You're Looking — Goldmann's 1945 Hemispherical Kinetic Bowl, Heijl & Krakau's 1975 Automated Blind-Spot Fixation & 20/20 Chiasmal Hemianopia
item.description: Psychophysics and neuro-ophthalmic anatomy of visual field perimetry: Goldmann's (1945) standardized luminance hemispherical bowl and kinetic target-velocity reaction-time artifact, Heijl & Krakau's (1975) automated computerized static threshold perimetry and blind-spot catch trials, and Ogra et al.'s (2014) proof that optic chiasm compression routinely produces bitemporal visual field loss despite 6/6 (20/20) foveal acuity.

item.title: How a Sleep Study Tells Why Breathing Stopped — Gastaut's 1965 Simultaneous EEG/Airflow/Effort Recording, Sullivan's 1981 Nasal CPAP Pneumatic Splint & PSG vs. Home Testing Denominators
item.description: Historical physiology of polysomnography and sleep-disordered breathing (H044): Gastaut, Tassinari & Duron's (1965–1966) polygraphic separation of obstructive, central, and mixed apneas by comparing airflow against thoracoabdominal effort, Sullivan et al.'s (1981) nasal CPAP pneumatic splint experiment, and the denominator divergence between EEG-verified total sleep time in polysomnography and recording/monitoring time in home sleep apnea testing (Bianchi & Goparaju 2017).

item.title: Why a Pinhole Can Sharpen a Blurry Letter — Snellen's 5-Arcminute Optotypes, Bailey-Lovie LogMAR Charts, Campbell & Gregory's 2 mm Aperture & Eagan's Retinal-Illumination Trap
item.description: Physiological optics of clinical visual acuity and refraction (H051): Snellen's (1862) 5-arcminute optotype standard, Bailey & Lovie's (1976) proportional logMAR chart design, Campbell & Gregory's (1960) tradeoff between geometrical blur circles and diffraction across pupil diameters, Eagan et al.'s (1999) demonstration of pinhole retinal-dimming pseudoworsening in maculopathy, and Donders (1864) / Sankaridurg et al. (2017) on cycloplegic vs. non-cycloplegic refraction.

item.title: How a Brain Recording Can Reveal a Response Without Movement — Owen's 2006 Tennis/Navigation fMRI Imagery, Sitt's 2014 EEG Complexity Markers & Claassen (2019) / Bodien (2024) Cognitive Motor Dissociation
item.description: Detecting covert command-following in behaviorally unresponsive brain-injured patients: Owen et al.'s (2006) fMRI mental-imagery paradigm, Sitt et al.'s (2014) quantitative EEG markers in disorders of consciousness, Claassen et al.'s (2019) bedside motor-command EEG classifier identifying cognitive motor dissociation and predicting 1-year functional recovery, and Bodien et al.'s (2024) six-center cohort quantifying both prevalence (25%) and negative-result sensitivity limits.

item.title: How a Newborn Hearing Screen Listens for an Answer — Jewett & Williston's 1971 Averaged ABR Waves, David Kemp's 1978 Outer-Hair-Cell Otoacoustic Emissions & Starr's 1996 Auditory Neuropathy Paradox
item.description: Objective physiological hearing screening without behavioral responses: Jewett & Williston's (1971) time-locked signal averaging of microvolt auditory brainstem responses (ABR), David Kemp's (1978) discovery of active cochlear outer-hair-cell otoacoustic emissions (OAE), NICU screening validation (Stevens et al. 1990), and Starr et al.'s (1996) discovery of auditory neuropathy with preserved OAEs and absent ABR.

item.title: How an Eye-Pressure Test Reads Through the Cornea — Schiøtz Indentation, Goldmann & Schmidt's 1957 3.06-mm Applanation Tear-Film & Corneal Stiffness Balance, Ehlers's Cannulated Eye Study & OHTS Corneal Thickness
item.description: Biomechanics of intraocular pressure measurement through the cornea (H052): Schiøtz (1905) indentation vs. Goldmann & Schmidt's (1957) small-area 3.06-mm applanation balancing tear-film capillarity against corneal stiffness, Ehlers et al.'s (1975) direct intracameral manometry demonstrating corneal thickness bias, and OHTS (2002) risk stratification.

item.title: How an Audiogram Finds Which Ear Heard the Tone — Fletcher & Wegel's 1922 Calibrated Thresholds, Transcranial Bone-Conduction Crossover, Denes & Naunton's Narrowband Noise & Hood's 1957 Masking Plateau
item.description: Acoustics and clinical logic of pure-tone audiometry and contralateral masking (H050): Fletcher & Wegel's (1922) calibrated receiver thresholds, skull-vibration crossover to the non-test cochlea, Denes & Naunton's (1952) frequency-band masking efficiency, and J.D. Hood's (1957) plateau method separating cross-heard responses from true ear-specific air- and bone-conduction thresholds.

item.title: How a Sea Slug Gets Used to a Touch — Pinsker's Aplysia Gill-Withdrawal Habituation, Castellucci & Kandel's 1974 Quantal Failure Analysis & Bailey & Chen's Electron-Microscopy Presynaptic Active Zones
item.description: From behavioral habituation to synaptic quantal release and ultrastructure in Aplysia: Pinsker et al.'s (1970) gill-withdrawal habituation and dishabituation, Castellucci & Kandel's (1974) quantal variance/failure proof that short-term habituation reflects fewer transmitter packets released per impulse rather than smaller postsynaptic unit responses, and Bailey & Chen's (1983) electron microscopy of long-term habituated sensory-neuron varicosities.

item.title: When the Same Taste Signal Leads to Opposite Choices — Chandrashekar's Dish Bitter Receptor Screen, Zhao & Mueller's RASSL Spiradoline Routing & Human TAS2R16 Expressed in Mouse Sweet vs. Bitter Cells
item.description: Labeled-line coding in mammalian taste: separating molecular ligand detection in heterologous cells (Chandrashekar et al. 2000; Bufe et al. 2002 TAS2R16) from behavioral attraction vs. aversion in mice when the exact same engineered receptor (spiradoline RASSL, Zhao 2003) or human bitter receptor (TAS2R16, Mueller 2005) is expressed in T1R2 sweet cells vs. T2R bitter cells.

item.title: Why a Fly's Eye Went Quiet in the Light — Cosens & Manning's 1969 Drosophila trp Mutant, Montell's Gene Rescue, Hardie & Minke's Ca2+-Selective Current, Niemeyer's trp/trpl Double Mutant & Asp621 Pore Selectivity
item.description: Discovery of the founding TRP ion channel in Drosophila vision: Cosens & Manning's (1969) transient receptor potential mutant fading in continuous light, Montell & Rubin's gene rescue and cloning, Hardie & Minke's (1992) single-photoreceptor patch-clamp proof of missing Ca2+ permeability, Niemeyer et al.'s (1996) trp/trpl dissection, and Liu et al.'s (2007) pore-selectivity mutagenesis.

item.title: How a Locust Turns Sound into Current — Michelsen's Abdominal Frequency Tuning, Windmill's Laser-Scanned Tympanum Waves, Warren's Auditory Receptor Currents & Chaiyasitdhi's 2-µm Axial Pull vs. Push
item.description: Biophysics of insect tympanal hearing in the desert locust: Michelsen's (1968) receptor frequency tuning, Windmill et al.'s (2008) laser-vibrometry frequency-sorting waves across the abdominal tympanum, Warren & Matheson's (2018) isolated transduction currents, and Chaiyasitdhi et al.'s (2025 reviewed preprint) direct 2-µm cap pull vs. push recordings.

item.title: How a Sour Taste Starts — Huang's PKD2L1 Sour-Cell Ablation, Chang's Apical Proton Current, Tu's Otop1 Proton Channel Cloning & Teng/Zhang's Chorda Tympani Nerve Loss in Otop1-/- Mice
item.description: From cell-type ablation to the molecular proton sensor for sour taste: Huang et al. (2006) selective elimination of PKD2L1 taste cells erasing chorda tympani acid responses while sparing sweet, salty, bitter, and umami, Chang, Waters & Liman (2010) direct measurement of apical proton entry, Tu et al. (2018) discovery of the OTOP1 proton channel, and Teng et al. / Zhang et al. (2019) in vivo Otop1-/- requirement for sour nerve signaling.

item.title: Why an Aroma Can Seem to Come from Your Mouth — Rozin's Dual-Olfaction Juice Test, Dalton's Subthreshold Saccharin-Benzaldehyde Integration, Small's Retronasal fMRI & Blankenship's Optogenetics
item.description: Neurobiology of retronasal olfaction and flavor referral: Rozin (1982) dual-sense hypothesis, Dalton et al. (2000) subthreshold benzaldehyde + saccharin integration (28% lower threshold vs. null MSG control), Small et al. (2005) nasal-cannula fMRI showing route-dependent brain activation for identical vapor concentrations, and Blankenship et al. (2019) gustatory cortex requirement for rapid retronasal learning.

item.title: How a Robin Reads the Tilt of a Magnetic Field — Wiltschko's 1972 Horizontal vs. Vertical Coil Flips, Ritz's Radio-Frequency Disruption & Xu's European Robin Cryptochrome 4
item.description: Biophysics of the avian inclination compass: Wiltschko & Wiltschko (1972) proof that European robins read magnetic field line dip angle (poleward vs. equatorward) rather than polarity, Ritz et al. (2004) diagnostic radio-frequency spin resonance disruption, and Xu et al. (2021) transient absorption spectroscopy of purified migratory European robin vs. non-migratory chicken/pigeon Cryptochrome 4.

item.title: When the Same Sound Becomes a Surprise — Sutton's P300 Uncertainty Cue, Bekinschtein's Local-vs.-Global Oddball Hierarchy & Wacongne's Omitted-Tone Prediction Error
item.description: Electrophysiology of auditory expectation and hierarchical prediction error: Sutton et al. (1965) P300 discovery comparing identical clicks under certainty vs. uncertainty, Bekinschtein et al. (2009) local-global paradigm where a locally Deviant XXXXX/XXXXY sequence becomes the global rule, and Wacongne et al. (2011) brain responses to an omitted expected tone.

item.title: How Light Sets the Body Clock — Rodless/Coneless Circadian Phase Shifts, Berson's Retrograde SCN Ganglion Cells, Melanopsin Knockout Rescue & Opn4Diphtheria Ablation
item.description: Discovery of intrinsically photosensitive retinal ganglion cells (ipRGCs): Freedman et al. (1999) intact circadian photoentrainment without rods and cones, Berson, Dunn & Takao (2002) intrinsic light responses in SCN-projecting ganglion cells after synaptic isolation, Hattar et al. (2003) triple-knockout loss of entrainment when rods, cones, and melanopsin are removed together, and Güler et al. (2008) ipRGC cell ablation.

item.title: A Sodium Channel for Pain and Smell — Cox's SCN9A (NaV1.7) Nonsense Variants, Patch-Clamp Loss of Current & Weiss's Olfactory Glomerular Synaptic Failure
item.description: How one voltage-gated sodium channel links nociception and olfaction: Cox et al. (2006) biallelic SCN9A (NaV1.7) truncations eliminating pain while sparing touch, and Weiss et al. (2011) dual recordings proving NaV1.7-null olfactory sensory neurons fire odor-evoked action potentials at the soma but fail to trigger synaptic transmission in the olfactory bulb glomerulus.

item.title: What an Eye Movement Can Tell Us About Dreaming — Aserinsky & Kleitman's 1953 EOG Awakenings, Dement's Duration Judgments, Foulkes's Definition Shift & Siclari's Posterior Hot Zone
item.description: From Aserinsky & Kleitman's (1953) discovery of Rapid Eye Movement sleep and Dement & Kleitman's (1957) 5-vs.-15-minute binary duration judgments to Foulkes's (1962) proof that NREM mental activity depends on definition thresholds and Siclari et al.'s (2017) posterior cortical low-frequency reduction predicting dream experience within both REM and NREM sleep.

item.title: How the Nose Builds an Odor Code — Buck & Axel's Olfactory Receptor Family, Zhao's Adenoviral I7 Pairing, Malnic's Combinatorial Code & Bozza's Bulb Glomeruli
item.description: Molecular logic of combinatorial olfaction: Buck & Axel (1991) cloning of the odorant receptor superfamily, Zhao et al. (1998) functional pairing of receptor I7 with octanal, Malnic et al. (1999) single-neuron calcium imaging + RT-PCR showing concentration-dependent recruitment (2 to 5 to 8 receptors for bromooctanoic acid), and Bozza et al. (2004) in vivo glomerular synapto-pHluorin maps.

item.title: How the Ear Turns Up Its Own Volume — Brownell's Outer Hair Cell Electromotility, Zheng's Prestin Discovery & Dallos's Stiffness-Preserving Knock-In
item.description: Biophysics of the cochlear amplifier: Brownell et al. (1985) voltage-driven length changes in guinea-pig outer hair cells, Zheng et al. (2000) subtractive cloning of prestin (SLC26A5), Liberman et al. (2002) 40–60 dB threshold shift in prestin-/- mice, and Dallos et al. (2008) 499-prestin knock-in separating active motor force from passive axial stiffness.

item.title: Why a Chili Pepper Feels Hot — Caterina & Julius's TRPV1 Expression-Cloning Screen, Thermal Activation, Knockout Hyperalgesia & Chicken-Rat Chimeras
item.description: Discovery and dissection of polymodal nociception via TRPV1: Caterina et al. (1997) Fura-2 expression cloning from dorsal root ganglia, physical heat (>43°C) gating of the capsaicin receptor, Caterina et al. (2000) TRPV1-/- loss of inflammatory thermal hyperalgesia, and Jordt & Julius (2002) separation of capsaicin and thermal gating in avian-mammalian chimeras.

item.title: A Chemical Signal Comes in Packets — Fatt & Katz Miniature Endplate Potentials, Del Castillo & Katz Poisson Quantal Failures & Heuser-Reese Quick-Freeze Exocytosis
item.description: Statistical and ultrastructural proof of quantal synaptic transmission: Fatt & Katz (1952) spontaneous miniature endplate potentials, del Castillo & Katz (1954) independent quantal content estimates (0.57 by amplitude ratio vs. 0.56 by Poisson failure fraction), and Heuser & Reese (1979) 3–5 ms quick-freeze electron microscopy.

item.title: How a Shark Finds a Fish Under Sand — Murray's Ampullae of Lorenzini Recordings, Kalmijn's Agar-Chamber & Dipole Strikes & Sawfish Electrosense
item.description: Experimental proof of passive electroreception in elasmobranchs: Murray (1962) ampullae of Lorenzini nerve recordings, Kalmijn (1971) catshark and skate strikes at agar-screened live plaice vs. polyethylene insulation vs. artificial bioelectric dipoles, and Wueringer et al. (2012) sawfish rostral electrosense.

item.title: When GABA Pulls Voltage the Other Way — KCC2 Chloride Extrusion, Gramicidin-Perforated Patch Anion Reversal & Microglial BDNF in Neuropathic Pain
item.description: Ionic basis of GABAergic polarity switches: Rivera et al. (1999) KCC2 antisense knockdown in hippocampal neurons, Coull et al. (2003, 2005) gramicidin-perforated patch recordings in spinal lamina I after nerve injury (-72.6 mV to -49.0 mV) driven by microglial BDNF-TrkB signaling, and depolarizing shunting conductance.

item.title: The Butterfly That Steers by a Clock — Monarch Phase-Shifted Flight Simulators, Antennal Circadian Clocks & Conflicting Black-vs.-Clear Enamel Inputs
item.description: Neuroethology of the monarch butterfly time-compensated sun compass: Mouritsen & Frost (2002) ±6h photoperiod shifts (225° vs. 136° vs. 335°), Merlin et al. (2009) antennal light-entrained circadian oscillators, and Guerra et al. (2012) rescue of group orientation by amputating a desynchronized black-painted antenna.

item.title: When One Eye Takes the Lead — Wiesel & Hubel's Monocular vs. Binocular Deprivation, Critical Period Timing & Pizzorusso's Perineuronal Net Chondroitinase
item.description: Synaptic competition and critical period closure in visual cortex: Wiesel & Hubel (1963–1970) why monocular suture shifts cortical drive (1/84 cells) while binocular suture preserves responsiveness, and Pizzorusso et al. (2002) extracellular matrix chondroitin sulfate proteoglycan digestion in adult rats.

item.title: How a Bat Measures the Dark — Pierce & Griffin's Ultrasonic Detector, Galambos's Obstacle Course & Simmons's Electronic Echo-Delay Target Illusion
item.description: Experimental discovery of bat echolocation: Pierce & Griffin (1938) ultrasonic heterodyne detector, Griffin & Galambos (1941) reversible sight vs. hearing vs. vocalization blocks, terminal buzz pursuit (1960), and Kick & Simmons (1984) electronic delay-line phantom targets.

item.title: How We Learned to Read a Cell: How a Touch Becomes a Current — Chick Muscle Stretch Channels (1984), Piezo1/2 RNAi Screen (2010) & Bilayer Reconstitution
item.description: On the Shoulders of Giants Historical Teaching Pilot 3: how Guharay & Sachs (1984), Coste et al. (2010, 2012), Ranade et al. (2014), and Syeda et al. (2016) proved that Piezo1 and Piezo2 are the bona fide pore-forming mechanosensitive ion channels underlying vertebrate gentle touch.

item.title: How We Learned to Read a Cell: A Flash in the Dark — Hecht-Shlaer-Pirenne Thresholds (1942), Baylor Single-Rod Suction Pipettes (1979) & cGMP Gating
item.description: On the Shoulders of Giants Historical Teaching Pilot 1: from Hecht, Shlaer & Pirenne's (1942) 5-14 photon human psychophysical threshold to Baylor, Lamb & Yau's (1979) 1 pA single-photon suction-pipette recordings in toad rod outer segments and Fesenko et al.'s (1985) inside-out patch cGMP gating proof.

item.description: Biochemical and analytical dissection of Maple Syrup Urine Disease (MSUD) decompensation: human BCKDH E1 alpha-ketoacid decarboxylation and BCKDK Ser292 phosphorylation (PDB 1DTW/1OLS/4H7Q), chromatographic separation of isobaric leucine, isoleucine, alloisoleucine, and hydroxyproline at m/z 132->86, LAT1 blood-brain barrier competition, IV BCAA-free rescue, and liver transplantation.

item.title: The Drug That Changed With the Fever — Clozapine 1975 Finland Cluster & Kane 1988 Trial, Human H4–Gi Structure (PDB 8JXV), CYP1A2 Inflammation/Smoking Shift & AGP Binding
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology Pilot 82: from the 1975 Finnish agranulocytosis cluster (Idänpään-Heikkilä et al.) and Kane et al.'s (1988) treatment-resistant schizophrenia trial (38/126 vs. 5/141) to ancillary human H4-Gi cryo-EM structure (PDB 8JXV), why acute pneumonia and abrupt smoking cessation elevate serum clozapine and the clozapine:norclozapine ratio via IL-6 CYP1A2 suppression and de-induction (Faber & Fuhr; Dickmann; Raaska), alpha-1-acid glycoprotein (AGP) unbound-fraction buffering, and the June 2025 FDA clozapine REMS removal.

item.title: The Pocket That Did Not Predict the Trial — Fragile X FMR1 Methylation PCR, Grm5 Rescue, Mavoglurant in Human mGlu5 (PDB 4OO9), [11C]ABP688 PET & FXLEARN
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology Pilot 79: FMR1 CGG repeat-primed and HpaII methylation PCR (Chen et al.), Fmr1 x Grm5 genetic cross (Dölen et al. 2007) and CTEP chronic rescue (Michalon et al. 2012), mavoglurant (AFQ056) bound 8 Å below the membrane surface in human mGlu5 (PDB 4OO9, Asn747/Ser805/Ser809), human [11C]ABP688 PET receptor occupancy, why Jacquemont's (2011) 7-person full-methylation subgroup failed prospective replication in Phase 2b (Berry-Kravis et al. 2016), and the FXLEARN pediatric language trial (log10 contrast -0.10, P=.16).

item.title: The Walk That Became a Seizure — Dalfampridine (4-AP) in Demyelinated Axons, Kv1.2/Kv2.1 Architecture (PDB 2R9R), Timed-Walk Trial Denominators & Renal Seizure Risk
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology Pilot 77: dalfampridine (4-aminopyridine) conduction rescue in diphtheria-toxin demyelinated rat spinal roots (Bostock, Sherratt & Sears 1978–1981), Kv1.2/Kv2.1 paddle-chimera selectivity filter coordinates (PDB 2R9R, Val371/Gly372), Goodman et al. (2009, 2010) Phase 3 timed 25-foot walk responder denominators (78/224 vs. 6/72; 51/119 vs. 11/118), extended-release vs. oral solution Cmax, and why renal impairment (CrCl <= 50 mL/min) precipitates acute seizures.

item.title: What the Hair Could Tell Us — Early Iron Age Tunnug 1 Cannabis Burial, Hair-Shaft CBN LC-HRMS/MS vs. Environmental Transfer, Human CB1-Gi1 Cryo-EM (PDB 9ERX) & Hallstatt Radiocarbon
item.description: Archaeotoxicology and receptor pharmacology of ancient cannabis at Tunnug 1 (Tuva, Early Iron Age): LC-HRMS/MS detection of cannabinol (CBN) in a preserved human hair braid alongside 965 botanical cannabis seeds, Hallstatt Plateau 14C calibration, human CB1-Gi1 cryo-EM structure (PDB 9ERX), forensic hair-testing boundaries between smoke/handling transfer and metabolic THC-COOH incorporation (Moosmann et al. 2015), and comparative Eurasian archaeobotany.

item.title: The Drug That Took the Long Way — Parkinson's Vallecular Tablet Retention on Videofluoroscopy, Enterococcus faecalis TyrDC Gut Decarboxylation & Oral vs. Jejunal Levodopa-Carbidopa Gel Kinetics
item.description: Mechanical and microbial bottlenecks along levodopa's route from mouth to brain: videofluoroscopic discovery of tablet retention in the valleculae (Sato et al. 2018), carbidopa-insensitive gut microbial tyrosine decarboxylase (Enterococcus faecalis TyrDC) and Eggerthella lenta dopamine dehydroxylase (Maini Rekdal et al. 2019; van Kessel et al. 2019), and oral vs. continuous jejunal infusion pharmacokinetics (Othman et al. 2015).

item.title: The Dose That Bought Another Hour — Parkinson's Levodopa Wearing-Off Diaries, Catechol-O-Methyltransferase (COMT) Mg2+ Coordination (PDB 7XGI), Opicapone Erythrocyte Kinetics, BIPARK-I & Tolcapone Hepatotoxicity
item.description: From Parkinson's wearing-off diaries to peripheral COMT inhibition: separating seated motor OFF time from orthostatic hypotension, competing AADC and COMT metabolic pathways, rat soluble COMT crystal structure bound to opicapone and Mg2+ (PDB 7XGI), plasma LC-MS/MS vs. sustained erythrocyte COMT inhibition kinetics, BIPARK-I/II trial endpoints, and tolcapone vs. opicapone hepatic safety.

item.title: The Pump at the Brain — Blood-Brain Barrier P-Glycoprotein (ABCB1) Efflux, Loperamide vs. Fentanyl CNS Exclusion, Cryo-EM ATPase Cycle & Drug-Drug Interactions
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology deep dive into blood-brain barrier ABCB1 (P-glycoprotein) efflux: why potent mu-opioid agonists like loperamide act peripherally unless P-gp is overwhelmed or inhibited, inward-to-outward cryo-EM peristaltic extrusion, and clinical transporter inhibition.

item.title: The Calabar Bean & the Missing Signal — Physostigmine, Acetylcholinesterase Ser203 Carbamylation, Antimuscarinic Delirium & QRS Counterfactuals
item.description: From Efik esere ordeal records in Old Calabar and Thomas Richard Fraser's Edinburgh experiments to human acetylcholinesterase Ser203 carbamylation (4EY4/1GQR), false-positive urine TCA immunoassays, and ECG QRS gating in antimuscarinic delirium.
